title: Vacancy Order and Physical Properties of a Ternary Compound Fe0.68Pd0.80Te with an α-Fe1+xTe-Type Structure
authors: Bingxian Shi, Manyu Wang, Chenglin Shang, Yanyan Geng, Yangyang Fan, Xiaoxiao Pei, Li Huang, Daye Xu, Juanjuan Liu, Jinchen Wang, Hongxia Zhang, Hongliang Wang, Lijie Hao, Rui Xu, Zhongyi Lu, Zhihai Cheng, Peng Cheng
abstract: We report the identification and characterization of a new compound Fe0.68Pd0.80Te with an α-Fe1+xTe prototype structure. Different from the Fe-square net and minor occupancy of interstitial Fe-sites in Fe1+xTe, Fe0.68Pd0.80Te is featured by a Pdsquare net and near 68% occupancy of the corresponding interstitial Fe-sites. Furthermore, noncontact atomic force microscopy and X-ray diffraction provide evidence for the existence of a 3*3*3 Pd-vacancy order in this layered material. A spin-glass ground state below Tg 40 K is identified via magnetic characterization. Electrical transport measurements show that Fe0.68Pd0.80Te is a semiconductor with a very small band gap below 10 meV. It has weak negative magnetoresistance and holelike charge carriers below room temperature. Our results demonstrate its potentials for further exploring various quantum phenomena.
summary: This paper reports the synthesis and detailed characterization of the novel compound Fe0.68Pd0.80Te. Key findings include the confirmation of a 3x3x3 vacancy superlattice and the identification of a spin-glass magnetic state below 40 K. Electrically, the material is characterized as a semiconductor with a very small band gap, suggesting potential for quantum electronic applications.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize a new ternary compound, Fe0.68Pd0.80Te, focusing on the role of vacancy ordering and its resulting physical properties.
main_result: The material exhibits a spin-glass ground state below 40 K, is a semiconductor with a very small band gap (< 10 meV), and possesses a confirmed 3x3x3 Pd-vacancy order.
method: The research employed a combination of structural characterization (XRD, nc-AFM), magnetic measurements (MPMS), and electrical transport measurements (PPMS-14T).
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered ternary compound Fe0.68Pd0.80Te, which adopts an alpha-Fe1+xTe-type tetragonal structure. The key structural feature is the presence of a vacancy-ordered superstructure, which influences its electronic and magnetic behavior.
key_observables: Spin-glass transition temperature (Tg ~ 40 K), semiconductor band gap (< 10 meV), hole-like charge carriers, and the 3x3x3 Pd-vacancy superlattice order.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), magnetic field (H), and the vacancy ordering parameter (3x3x3).
main_assumptions: The structural refinement assumes the material maintains a tetragonal structure despite significant chemical substitution and vacancy ordering. The small band gap suggests semiconductor behavior.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns confirming the structure, magnetic susceptibility curves demonstrating a spin-glass state, and resistivity vs. temperature plots indicating semiconducting behavior.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard materials science structure: structural identification and characterization (XRD, AFM) $ightarrow$ magnetic property measurement (Spin-glass state) $ightarrow$ electronic transport analysis (Semiconducting gap, MR/Hall effect) $ightarrow$ Conclusion on quantum potential.
why_interesting: The combination of vacancy ordering (a form of structural disorder) leading to a spin-glass state and semiconducting behavior makes it relevant for studying disorder-induced quantum phenomena in layered materials.
